originalTitle: Are Midterm Elections a headwind for stocks?
summary: Investing.com -- Investor attention is set to shift toward the U.S. midterm elections over the coming months, with Goldman Sachs expecting rising policy uncertainty and market volatility ahead of the November vote, while arguing that the election outcome itself is unlikely to be a major driver of equity performance.
content:
Investing.com -- Investor attention is set to shift toward the U.S. midterm elections over the coming months, with Goldman Sachs expecting rising policy uncertainty and market volatility ahead of the November vote, while arguing that the election outcome itself is unlikely to be a major driver of equity performance.

The brokerage said U.S. equities have historically traded sideways in the months leading up to midterm elections, with the S&P 500 posting a median return of 0% between the start of August and Election Day since 1974. However, returns have typically strengthened after the vote as uncertainty fades, with the index delivering a median gain of 6% over the following three months.

Goldman said economic policy uncertainty and equity volatility usually rise during the late summer before midterm elections, prompting mutual funds and foreign investors to trim exposure to U.S. equities before rebuilding positions after the vote. It added that the current backdrop of unusually low stock correlations makes owning equity index volatility increasingly attractive as investors shift their focus from earnings to macroeconomic issues including elections, geopolitics and interest-rate movements.

The bank also warned that rising Treasury yields could add further pressure on equities. It noted that stocks have historically struggled when 10-year Treasury yields rise by more than two standard deviations over a month, equivalent to roughly a 50-basis-point increase under current market conditions.

Despite the heightened attention on the elections, Goldman believes the result is unlikely to trigger major legislative surprises. Prediction markets imply roughly an 85% probability that Democrats will regain control of the House, while the Senate remains close to a toss-up, limiting the scope for unexpected policy shifts. Instead, investors are expected to focus on what the results could signal for the 2028 presidential election and future policy direction.

The report said inflation remains the dominant voter concern this election cycle, with surveys showing prices outranking other issues. Investors are also closely watching potential implications for artificial intelligence regulation, which polling suggests enjoys bipartisan support.

Goldman found little evidence that shifts in election probabilities have materially affected most sectors or investment themes in recent months. Consumer discretionary stocks have shown the strongest, though still modest, relationship with changing election odds, while the broader market has largely remained driven by other factors.

chineseTitle: 中期选举对股市来说是逆风吗？
chineseSummary: Investing.com——未来几个月，投资者的注意力将转向美国中期选举，高盛预计11月投票前政策不确定性和市场波动性将上升，同时认为选举结果本身不太可能成为股市表现的主要驱动力。
chineseContent:
Investing.com——未来几个月，投资者的注意力将转向美国中期选举，高盛预计11月投票前政策不确定性和市场波动性将上升，同时认为选举结果本身不太可能成为股市表现的主要驱动力。

该券商表示，从历史上看，美国股市在中期选举前的几个月里一直横盘整理，自 1974 年以来，标准普尔 500 指数从 8 月初到选举日期间的中位回报率为 0%。然而，随着不确定性的消退，投票后回报率通常会有所加强，该指数在接下来的三个月内的中位涨幅为 6%。

高盛表示，经济政策不确定性和股市波动性通常会在中期选举前的夏末上升，促使共同基金和外国投资者在投票后重建头寸之前削减对美国股市的投资。它补充说，当前股票相关性异常低的背景使得拥有股票指数波动性变得越来越有吸引力，因为投资者将注意力从收益转向包括选举、地缘政治和利率变动在内的宏观经济问题。

该银行还警告称，美国国债收益率上升可能会给股​​市带来进一步压力。报告指出，从历史上看，当10年期国债收益率在一个月内上涨超过两个标准差时，股市就会陷入困境，相当于在当前市场条件下上涨约50个基点。

尽管选举受到高度关注，但高盛认为结果不太可能引发重大立法意外。市场预测，民主党将重新获得众议院控制权的可能性约为 85%，而参议院仍将难以抉择，从而限制了意外政策转变的范围。相反，预计投资者将关注结果可能对 2028 年总统选举和未来政策方向发出的信号。

报告称，通胀仍然是选民在本次选举周期中最关心的问题，调查显示价格问题比其他问题更重要。投资者也在密切关注人工智能监管的潜在影响，民意调查显示该监管得到了两党的支持。

高盛发现，几乎没有证据表明选举概率的变化对近几个月的大多数行业或投资主题产生了重大影响。非必需消费品股票与不断变化的选举赔率的关系表现出最强（尽管仍然温和）的关系，而大盘在很大程度上仍然受到其他因素的推动。
